msg: If you die without a will in Florida, the state decides who gets your assets under Florida's intestacy laws. Learn who inherits, what happens to your home, and how to protect your family.

Florida offers some of the strongest asset protection laws in the nation — unlimited homestead protection, LLC charging order exclusivity, tenancy by the entireties, and Domestic Asset Protection Trusts. Learn how to use them.
Florida has no state estate tax and no inheritance tax. Learn what that means for your heirs, how the federal estate tax exemption of $15 million applies in 2026, and which taxes still matter.
After years of Florida practice, these are the 10 estate planning mistakes we see most — and every one of them is avoidable.
Florida irrevocable trusts provide asset protection, Medicaid planning, estate tax reduction, and legacy control that revocable trusts cannot. Learn which type is right for your goals.
Florida law (F.S. 736.0408) lets you create a legally enforceable pet trust to care for your animals after you die. Learn how pet trusts work, what to fund, and how to set one up.
What a Florida revocable living trust is, how it avoids probate, what it costs, and how to fund it. A complete guide for Florida homeowners and families, with statute citations.
How much does a will cost in Florida? Real 2026 numbers — and how to make sure 'affordable' doesn't mean 'invalid.'
A step-by-step guide to making a valid will in Florida: signing requirements, two-witness rule, self-proving affidavits, electronic wills, and what happens if you die without one.
Why we built Cornerstone and the Florida Estate Kit — to help Floridians and new arrivals get their wills and trusts right under Florida law.
Retired in Florida? Here's how to protect your home and savings — and spare your family the probate maze.
How payable-on-death and transfer-on-death accounts let Florida assets avoid probate without a trust — plus why Florida has no TOD deed for real estate, and the risks of relying on beneficiary forms.
Second marriages and stepchildren make Florida estate planning complex. Learn how the elective share, homestead, and QTIP trusts protect both your spouse and your children.
Splitting time between Florida and another state? Your out-of-state will and trust may not work in Florida. Learn what snowbirds and new Florida residents must do to protect their estates.
A Florida land trust keeps your name off public property records, avoids probate, and simplifies ownership transfers. Learn how land trusts work under F.S. § 689.071 and who needs one.
If you have a living trust, you need a pour-over will too. Here's the safety net that catches anything left out of your trust.

Leaving money directly to a disabled beneficiary in Florida can disqualify them from SSI and Medicaid. A Special Needs Trust preserves their inheritance without affecting benefits. Learn how Florida SNTs work.
What makes a will legally valid in Florida — witness rules, capacity, self-proving affidavits — plus why handwritten wills fail and how wills are contested.
A Lady Bird deed lets you pass Florida real property to heirs at death without probate, while keeping full control during your lifetime. Learn how it works and when to use one.

A warranty deed guarantees clear title; a quitclaim deed transfers only whatever interest the grantor has, with no guarantees. Learn the difference, when to use each, and Florida's deed and documentary stamp tax rules.
A Florida attorney's guide to estate planning for business owners — succession, buy-sell agreements, trusts, and keeping your company out of probate.
Cryptocurrency, NFTs, online accounts, and digital files must be planned for or they may be lost forever. Learn how Florida's RUFADAA law governs digital asset inheritance and what to do now.
A step-by-step Florida estate planning checklist covering the five core documents every Florida resident needs, what each one does, and how to get started.

Florida guardianship is a costly, court-supervised process that strips a person of their legal rights. Learn how it works under Chapter 744 — and how a power of attorney and healthcare surrogate can avoid it entirely.
Wondering what a living trust actually costs in Florida? Here's a straight breakdown of attorney fees vs. flat-fee options — and what should be included.
Florida probate costs 3–5% of your gross estate and takes 6–18 months. Learn exactly what probate costs, how long it takes, and the three ways to avoid it entirely.

Tenancy by the entireties lets married Florida couples own property together with built-in creditor protection and automatic survivorship. Learn how it works for real estate and bank accounts, and its limits.
Florida probate is public, slow, and costly — but most of it is avoidable. Six proven ways to keep your estate out of the court system.
Just moved to Florida? Your out-of-state will or trust may not work the way you think. Here's the checklist every new resident should run through.
In Florida, a will alone forces your family through probate — a public court process costing 3–5% of your estate. Learn when a trust is the better choice for Florida residents.
New parents: the most important thing your will does isn't about money — it's naming who would raise your children. Here's what to put in place.
A Florida durable power of attorney must meet strict statutory requirements under F.S. Chapter 709. Learn what makes a POA valid, what powers it grants, and the mistakes that can make it useless.
Florida estate planning costs vary widely — from $1,500 for a basic will package to $5,000+ at traditional firms. Here is exactly what you should pay and what you get for your money.
A Florida healthcare surrogate designates who makes medical decisions if you cannot. A living will states your end-of-life wishes. Learn the requirements, differences, and why you need both.
Florida Medicaid has a 60-month lookback period. Transfers made within 5 years of applying can cause disqualification. Learn how to protect your assets legally before it's too late.
Florida probate typically takes 6 to 12 months for formal administration and 4 to 8 weeks for summary administration. Learn the steps, the timeline, the costs, and how to avoid probate entirely.
When the grantor dies, the successor trustee must follow specific Florida legal steps. Here is the complete trust administration timeline, duties, and pitfalls to avoid under Florida law.
How to update, change, or revoke a will in Florida — codicils vs. new wills, revocation by act, what divorce does automatically, and when you should review your plan.
Florida legally recognizes electronic wills signed and witnessed online. Learn how Florida's electronic will law works, the remote notarization rules, and when an online will is right for you.
Will your family inherit your debt in Florida? The answer is usually reassuring — here's how it actually works.
Not married? In Florida, your partner has no automatic right to inherit or make medical decisions for you. Here's how to protect each other.
In Florida, a surviving spouse is entitled to 30% of the elective estate — even if the will leaves them nothing. Learn how the elective share works, what assets count, and how to plan around it.

Married couples in Florida face unique estate planning decisions — joint trust vs. separate trusts, spousal elective share, homestead restrictions, and Medicaid planning. Here is what every Florida couple needs to know.

Florida's homestead laws provide powerful tax savings and creditor protection — but also strict inheritance restrictions. Learn how homestead affects your estate plan and how to transfer your home into a trust correctly.
What a Florida personal representative (executor) does, who can legally serve, the out-of-state residency restriction, and how fees are set under Florida law.
Florida probate is a public court process; trust administration is private and faster. Compare the cost, timeline, and steps of each, and learn what your family will actually face.
Florida Estate Kit creates a complete, attorney-reviewed estate plan online — revocable living trust, will, power of attorney, and healthcare documents — starting from $699.
Created a living trust? If you never funded it, it avoids nothing. Here's how to actually move your assets into your Florida trust.
Should you use an online service, hire a traditional Florida attorney, or do both? A side-by-side comparison of cost, Florida-law accuracy, and risk — and the attorney-reviewed middle path.
